surprises.head: The Rangers shut down Edmonton’s power play
surprises.body: Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years. Not tonight: 2.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 9.5 and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Levi robs the Rangers
paras: Connor McDavid opened the scoring for the Oilers early in the first. Leon Draisaitl pushed the lead to 2-0 early in the second, and the goal stood after the Rangers challenged for goalie interference, and that one stood up as the winner. Jaroslav Chmelař got the Rangers on the board shorthanded just over two minutes later. The Oilers went more than 16 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the second to early in the third, while the Rangers put ten on net. Draisaitl scored his second of the night into the empty net with a little over a minute left, his fourth straight game with a goal.

The Rangers had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Rangers win about seven in ten. Devon Levi made the difference in net, stopping 30 of 31. Dylan Garand stopped 17 of 19 for the Rangers.

Three players picked up ten-minute misconducts. Neither power play scored: the Oilers killed all five Rangers power plays, and the Rangers killed all three of Edmonton’s. The Oilers moved to 13-3-3, still first in the Pacific, while the Rangers dropped to 10-8-1, third in the Metropolitan.
